old: Long ago, English had its own homegrown word for this idea, but it lost ground to a newcomer.
The word that replaced it traces to a Latin root meaning wide, spacious, or able to hold a lot.
That Latin root, capāx, is a cousin of the word capable — both about having room or ability to hold.
clues: This adjective about size and room pushed out a native Old English word, numol, which had once covered much the same ground.
It describes something roomy enough to hold a great deal, like a deep handbag or a vast closet, and sounds more formal than plain roomy.
Admirers might use it to praise a scholar's huge memory, and it shares its Latin root with capable: both point to being able to hold much.
